_purpose: S8's negative control consumes THIS file, never tools/rail_hue_breaches.json. Ruled by Matt 2026-08-14. A gate's proof-that-it-can-fail must not depend on a real breach happening to exist: when the last live breach was retired the old S8 would have failed on 'no recorded breach to exercise the control against' - a control that stops working because the estate got healthier. That is the same vacuity family as counting a crash as a rejection (register species 35). So the control gets a committed synthetic breach of its own, and the live record is free to be empty.
_notLive: Nothing here is a ruling about any real game. The two hrefs are deliberately fictional so this file can never be mistaken for the live record, and so a pair listed here can never silently excuse a real sub-floor collision on the rail. S3 does not read this file.
_pairIsSubFloor: The fixture pair measures dE00 2.25 against the rail floor of 25, and S8 re-measures it every run: a fixture whose pair stopped being sub-floor would make the control inert without saying so, so S8 fails rather than passes if that ever happens.

breaches.evidence: Committed control data, not an estate ruling. Exists so S8 can prove the breach-record mechanism refuses an unrecorded pair and refuses a recorded pair whose hue has moved, on a run where the live record is empty.
